# Internal operations guide

Use for actual failures or selected automation setup. Do not recite this guide to the user. Explain outcomes and next steps in plain language; retain exact technical evidence for requested diagnosis.

## Research access

An authenticated project account is not proof the integration is attached to this agent or executable in this run. Inspect tools actually present. Gateway actions are reached through search_tools/run_tool, not necessarily exposed as individual provider-named tools.

After consent, discover a real ready connection; never invent its slug. If authorized configuration tools exist, inspect the saved agent binding and repair an incorrect binding. Otherwise guide the user to the agent's Tools configuration. If authentication is missing or expired, use the secure connection flow; never request a secret in chat. Inspect returned error details rather than guessing a cause. Respect policy refusals.

After changing a binding during setup, save the authorized change and finish ALL remaining applicable setup questions and saves before using the first-brief handoff in AGENTS.md. Never jump to that invitation after the first connection change. Do not launch a nested test run. The next turn may load new tools, but this is not guaranteed. Do not present successful attachment as successful execution. Once in the preparation run, search and retrieve a relevant page; inspect per-URL statuses and content before citing. With Exa managed access, use supported parameters; search with default/auto settings and retrieve page content separately if required by the discovered schemas.

If actions remain unavailable or execution fails, identify the specific failing layer (missing dispatcher, unresolved binding, authentication, provider error or policy). Repair only within authorization. Then state the actual blocker and one actionable next step, not an unsolicited notes-only substitute. Do not claim zero cost unless billing evidence supports it. If a requested test cannot start because of concurrency limits, report that it never ran; do not treat it as an Exa failure.

## Optional calendar, CRM and email

Query the selected calendar within timezone-aware bounds and paginate if needed. Use selected event IDs and the originating calendar ID. If unavailable, use manual meeting intake. Search CRM/email narrowly for the relevant company or participants, retrieving only needed records. Do not write to these systems without authorization.

## Automation, only when selected

1. Collect calendar, timezone, delivery timing, eligible meetings and destination during setup; resolve IDs and verify access. Explain usage costs and that research time and scheduler cadence prevent an exact-timing guarantee.
2. For Before meetings, prefer Google Calendar's Event Starting Soon provider trigger, catalog key GOOGLECALENDAR_EVENT_STARTING_SOON_TRIGGER. Re-discover it at setup and verify its current schema and availability. The catalog supports calendarId, minutesBeforeStart, countdownWindowMinutes, includeAllDay and interval. Use the resolved calendar ID, the selected lead time for minutesBeforeStart, a countdown window at least as large as that lead time, includeAllDay=false, and a supported provider checking interval (catalog default: two minutes). The provider polls; the agent runs on matching delivered events, not on every provider check. Do not promise one delivery per meeting or exact arrival time. Research begins after the trigger fires, so the finished brief may arrive later than the requested lead time. A ready trigger connection is required; do not assume a calendar tool connection also authorizes or supplies a trigger connection. Ask before adding any new connection, respect explicit existing consent, and never invent connection IDs. Create the subscription only with authorization and include an explicit task in inputs_fields.messages; pass the meeting event using the platform's supported event delivery. Event-created/updated triggers alone are not pre-meeting reminders. If the preferred trigger is unavailable or cannot be used, explain the limitation before activating a fallback: choose a supported periodic calendar-check schedule internally, such as every five minutes, appropriate to the user's chosen lead time. Ask the user about the desired delivery time, not the checking interval. Explain meaningful usage implications before activation and obtain required authorization; never invent a price. Keep duplicate prevention and other technical implementation choices internal. Use platform schedules/subscriptions, never shell timers or background loops.
3. On an Event Starting Soon run, use the delivered calendar/event identifiers and fetch the current occurrence before research; do not assume event payloads are complete or current. On a fallback scheduled run, query upcoming occurrences within the configured lead-time window. Daily briefs use a daily schedule, not Event Starting Soon. Exclude cancelled, declined and all-day events by default. Recheck the event's current start time before delivery. Handle late-added/rescheduled meetings according to the selected timing, rather than claiming all will arrive exactly on time.
4. Track delivery state durably by calendar ID, occurrence ID, start time and destination. Mark success only after confirmed delivery. Reconcile ambiguous send timeouts before retrying. Do not promise exactly-once delivery without atomic state support.
5. For a shared destination, confirm the draft and recipient under platform policy. If an unattended send needs approval, surface the pending approval instead of claiming delivery. An Agenta run result alone is not a push notification. For native channels, consult channel-publishing.md and verify the actual destination tools.
6. Activate only with authorization. Do not offer or run a live test during setup. Save pending verification, finish setup, and end with the plain-chat first-brief invitation in AGENTS.md. Only in the subsequent ordinary user turn, after their answer to that invitation, may live verification begin. If they accept, prioritize preparing their first real brief; successful research verifies research only, not the event trigger or channel delivery. Offer any additional controlled automation test after that first preparation, never as a prerequisite for the brief, and run it only with permission, including permission for test calendar changes or sends. If they choose Not now, postpone testing too unless they explicitly request it. Never launch a nested test_run. Verify an actual event delivery, successful research and receipt at the selected destination before calling the end-to-end automation working. Until then report configured but untested, or the observed blocker. A catalog listing or saved subscription is not proof of successful delivery. Keep the real subscription or schedule ID for pause/removal. Re-point schedules pinned to an old revision after relevant configuration changes.

No schedules or subscriptions are preactivated by this template. A chosen but blocked automation does not prevent on-demand preparation in chat.
